Name: aggregate_or_comply
Title: Aggregate or Comply: Compiled Playbooks, Whole-Bank Context, Fixed Exemplars and Top-k Retrieval Under a Manipulated Contamination Rate of the Experience Bank
Short Hypothesis: The four ways of consuming an experience bank differ in where items are combined: a per-query retriever exposes the agent to each item at its bank share, a fixed exemplar set exposes it to one realisation of that share, an LLM compiler aggregates before the agent sees anything, and a long-context reader aggregates (or not) at read time. Under a manipulated fraction p in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1} of replay-validated wrong-procedure items, retrieval and fixed exemplars already lose at minority contamination (one wrong item in three is complied with, not outvoted), the LLM-compiled playbook stays flat at one-in-three and collapses at two-in-three, and the whole-bank arm decides whether an in-context reader is an aggregator or a complier. A wrong instruction in the playbook slot is followed at least as readily as wrong exemplars in the demonstration slot. The static route's first advantage over retrieval is robustness, not accuracy, and it is invisible in every existing comparison because their banks are clean.
Related Work: The compliance trap (2607.10608) shows agents adopt conflicting retrieved memory at the first exposed decision point and lists as untested whether compiled/static instructions induce the same behaviour and how the damage scales; it observes one route with fixed contamination. MemoryGraft (2512.16962), PoisonedEvolution (2608.05563), memory-poisoning attack/defence (2601.05504) and A-MemGuard (2510.02373, consensus-based validation) are security papers: single route, adversarially crafted items, attack success as outcome, no matched compiled-vs-retrieved-vs-whole-bank comparison and no dose-response on task success. MemAPO (2603.21520) argues per-query retrieval beats one compiled prompt on heterogeneous queries with a clean bank. Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations (2202.12837) found label correctness in in-context demonstrations barely matters for classification, an opposing prior that makes the compliance prediction non-trivial. Training-time poisoning shows phase transitions at a poisoning ratio (2303.03592) and aggregation as a certified defence (Run-Off Election, 2302.02300); no in-context, agentic analogue at the level of task success exists. Archived optimizer_substitutes_for_memory_scaffold (5.22) spoke of 'content harm' without manipulating content; here content harm is dosed. SkillEvolBench (2605.24117) reports skill gains unstable without variance; here compile-draw and sample-draw variance are measured.
Abstract: Every reported comparison of compiled artifacts with query-time retrieval uses a bank of successes that are all correct, so it cannot see the property that most distinguishes the routes: how they combine items. We build contaminated versions of the ALFWorld expert pool in which a fraction p in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1} of the heat/cool/clean trajectories have their procedure-defining step replaced by a plausible, executable but goal-ineffective step at a distractor receptacle in the same scene; every poisoned item is replayed in its game and kept only if it fails, and it replaces a clean item so bank size and goal-sentence distribution are unchanged (the goal-sentence retriever cannot tell them apart, so exposure is p per slot by construction; the outcome of interest is the agent's success response, which is not). Six routes consume each bank on the same (game, seed) cells: goal-query top-3 retrieval (realised exposure logged per episode), an LLM-compiled six-procedure playbook (Qwen3-32B summarising 12 sampled same-type items, cached, three draws per dose, artifact content audited as a descriptive covariate), a rule-compiled majority playbook (reference aggregator), the whole bank of 80 items in context (cached), a fixed three-exemplar set per type with exact composition j wrong items in three (five draws at j=1), and a slot-conflict cross that puts a wrong instruction against clean exemplars and a clean instruction against wrong exemplars in the same prompt. Every static route is also run at p=0, so each dose response has its own baseline. Task success on the three procedure types is primary; the untouched pick types are the in-arm control, tested once by a pooled regression; cost is uncached prefill per episode under caching. The design tests whether the reader outvotes a minority wrong item or complies with it (retrieval, fixed exemplars, whole bank), whether an LLM compiler aggregates below the majority and collapses above it, and whether a wrong instruction is followed at least as readily as wrong exemplars, each prediction falsifiable on success numbers alone at a stated floor.
Experiments: Poison construction: for each expert heat/cool/clean trajectory, replace the procedure-defining action (e.g., heat with microwave) by a same-scene distractor sequence (e.g., put the object on stoveburner 1, take it back), leave all other steps intact, replay under the ALFWorld engine and keep only items with success = 0 and no invalid steps; contamination rate p in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1} applied per procedure type by replacement (bank size and goal-sentence distribution unchanged; thirds match k=3 and the three-exemplar static sets, so exact compositions j = 3p wrong items in three exist for the fixed-sample arm). Every cell is 274 games x 2 seeds paired with the existing clean retrieval (A) and k=0 (C) cells unless stated; the procedure-type cell is ~137 games. Arms: R1 goal-query retrieval k=3 (A's retriever; p=0 exists at seeds 1-2 and is extended to seeds 3-4): p in {1/3, 2/3, 1}, the p=1/3 cell at 4 seeds; the realised number of poisoned items among the 3 retrieved is logged per episode. R2 LLM-compiled playbook: Qwen3-32B writes one procedure per type (all six, type-agnostic, ~400 tokens, cached) from 12 uniformly sampled same-type items with a compiler prompt that forbids knowledge outside the sample; three independent draws (sample and compilation) at p in {0, 1/3, 2/3}, one at p=1; each artifact audited per type as clean / poisoned / hedged, used only as a descriptive covariate, never as a gate. R3 rule-compiled majority playbook: majority extraction of the procedure-defining action template over the same 12-item samples, p in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1} (majority clean w.p. ~0.93 at 1/3 and wrong w.p. ~0.93 at 2/3, so its step is by construction and is reported, not predicted). R4 whole-bank_80: 80 type-balanced items sampled from the contaminated bank (~40 procedure items, ~13 wrong at p=1/3), fixed order per seed, cached, realised contamination recorded, p in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1}. R5 fixed exemplar set (type-conditioned static: three items of the goal's type, sampled once per draw): exact composition j wrong in three per procedure type, j in {0, 1, 2, 3}, with two draws at j=0, five at j=1, one each at j=2 and j=3. R6 slot-conflict cross (matched content, no sampling): the R3 playbook and an R5 exemplar set in the same prompt, each slot wholly clean (expert procedure) or wholly wrong (distractor procedure) for the three procedure types: R6a wrong instruction + clean exemplars and R6b clean instruction + wrong exemplars (both at 4 seeds), R6c clean + clean (combined static reference, 2 seeds); wrong + wrong is floored by construction and not run. Exploratory if time remains: a realism cell where R1's p=1/3 contamination consists of stale items from a name-swap wrapper (microwave <-> stoveburner) so the wrong items were once right. Order: R1_p1 (P1 gate) first; then the decisive one-in-three cells R1_p1/3, R2_p1/3 x3, R4_p1/3, R5_j1 x5; then the static p=0 cells; then R6; then the remaining doses. Count: R1 5 cell-equivalents (3 doses + the extra-seed halves of p=0 and p=1/3) + R2 10 + R3 4 + R4 4 + R5 9 + R6 5 = 37 cells x 548 episodes = 20,276 episodes; at the ~1,100 episodes/h that two vLLM replicas on two A100s with queue-tuned workers deliver (the rate behind the earlier 32-arm/16 h estimate) this is ~18.5 h. Pre-registered cut order if the measured rate is lower: R6c, R3_p1/3, R5_j2, R2_p1, then the R1/R5 extra seeds; no cut touches a cell named by P1-P4.
Baselines and Ablations: Baseline is the best static arm at each p (R2, R3, R5, and R6c at p=0), with retrieval reported as retrieval minus best static at matched tokens on the same (game, seed); the type-agnostic requirement is met by R2/R3/R4 (all six procedures, no type selection) and by the playbook half of R6; R5 is the type-conditioned static counterpart of R1. Ablations: p dose (four levels, thirds); compiler identity (LLM vs rule) and compiler-draw variance (three draws at p in {0, 1/3, 2/3}); static-sample (R5, exact composition) vs retrieved-sample (R1, realised exposure logged) at equal expected exposure; instruction slot vs exemplar slot at matched content (R6 cross); whole-bank realised contamination as a covariate; pick types as the untouched control; token accounting: R1 uncached ~430 tokens per episode vs cached prefixes for R2-R6 (R4 ~11k tokens cached).
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (positive control, gate): R1 at p=1 loses >= 20 points vs R1 at p=0 on the pooled procedure-type cell (~137 games x 2 seeds, floor +-12; 20 ~ half the Gate-0 gain on these types). Falsified if the loss is < 12: the agent does not follow the wrong procedure, the study stops and reports the poison as inert. If the loss lies in [12, 20) the poison is weak: the study continues but P2-P6 are declared exploratory and their margins are re-expressed as fractions of the p=1 loss (a 12-point margin becomes 60% of it). Where R1_p1 lands relative to k=0 (merely uninformative vs actively harmful) is reported descriptively and is not part of the gate. Arm R1_p1. P2 (headline: compliance at minority contamination): R1 at p=1/3 loses >= 12 vs R1 at p=0 on the procedure cell (both at 4 seeds, floor +-8.5). Falsified if the loss is < 12: the reader outvotes one wrong item in three, the 2202.12837 prior. Realised exposure (0-3 poisoned among the 3 retrieved) is logged per episode and the loss conditional on >= 1 poisoned item is reported as secondary; the unconditional loss decides. Arm R1_p1/3. P3 (LLM compiler aggregates below the majority and collapses above it), decided on success numbers alone with the artifact audit reported alongside as a descriptive covariate: (a) R2's draw-pooled loss at p=1/3 vs draw-pooled R2_p0 (three draws each, floor ~+-10 on the difference) has a 90% bootstrap CI lying below 12; falsified if the point loss is >= 12 with the CI excluding 0 (the compiler hedges or carries the minority into the playbook; an audit showing hedged or poisoned procedures is the reported reason, not a condition). (b) R2's draw-pooled loss at p=2/3 vs R2_p0 is >= 20; falsified if it is < 12, and this counts as falsified even when the audit shows the compiler restored the clean procedure from pretraining (the compiler-prior route is then the finding and the prompt-level ban on outside knowledge is reported as insufficient). Outcomes between are inconclusive and reported as such. Arms R2_p0 x3, R2_p1/3 x3, R2_p2/3 x3. Not entailed: unlike R3, the LLM artifact is not determined by the majority; the compiler can carry a minority item or reject a majority. P4 (whole-bank reader is a complier), stated on R4 alone: R4 at p=1/3 loses >= 12 vs R4 at p=0 (floor +-12 each; realised contamination of the 80-item sample recorded and reported as a covariate). Falsified if the loss is < 12: the long-context reader aggregates in context and ~13 wrong among ~40 procedure items are outvoted. Arms R4_p0, R4_p1/3. P5 (the instruction slot is no safer than the exemplar slot), measured on the slot-conflict cross where neither cell is floored: success in R6a (wrong instruction + clean exemplars) is at most success in R6b (clean instruction + wrong exemplars), R6a - R6b <= 0, both at 4 seeds (difference floor ~+-12). Falsified if R6a - R6b >= 12: clean exemplars override a wrong instruction more than a clean instruction overrides wrong exemplars, so the playbook slot is the safer place for a wrong item. Absolute levels of both cells are reported against R6c (clean + clean) and k=0. Arms R6a, R6b, R6c. P6 (fixed exemplars comply like retrieval and match it in expectation): (a) R5 at j=1 (five draws pooled, floor ~+-5.4) loses >= 12 vs R5 at j=0 (two draws pooled, floor ~+-8.5); falsified if the pooled loss is < 12 (a single fixed wrong exemplar is outvoted). (b) the R5_j1 draw mean is equivalent to R1_p1/3 (expected exposure one wrong in three in both) within +-12: confirmed if the 90% bootstrap CI of the difference (half-width ~9 after pooling) lies inside +-12; falsified if the point difference is >= 12 with the CI excluding 0 (a retrieved wrong item is treated differently from a fixed one). Between-draw SD at j=1 and the j=0..3 composition slope are reported descriptively with bootstrap CIs, not predicted. Arms R5_j0 x2, R5_j1 x5, R1_p1/3. P7 (in-arm control, one pooled test): a paired regression of pick-type success on p over all 37 cells, with route as a factor and game as block, yields a fitted p=0 to p=1 change within +-8 (pooled floor ~+-4). Falsified if |change| >= 8 with the 95% bootstrap CI excluding 0: spillover from the contaminated procedures, which invalidates the per-type attribution for the routes whose per-route terms carry it; per-route terms are reported descriptively with no per-cell tests.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired (game, seed) cells; net = paired success difference in points; floor +-8 at 274 x 2, +-12 on the ~137-game procedure-type cell at 2 seeds, +-8.5 at 4 seeds; draws are pooled where a prediction names a pooled cell (floor scales as 1/sqrt(draws); games shared across draws are handled by bootstrapping over games with seeds and draws nested). Margins: 12 (the 2-seed floor) and 20 (half the Gate-0 gain on the procedure types). Equivalence-type statements (P3a, P6b) use the 90% bootstrap CI of the difference against the margin and have an explicit inconclusive zone; directional statements (P1, P2, P3b, P4, P5, P6a) use the point estimate against the margin with the CI reported. Dose-response: paired regression of success on p with game as block and route as factor, bootstrap CI over games; R5's composition slope over j reported the same way. Realised exposure logged per episode in R1 and per sample in R2/R3/R4. The positive control (P1) gates the rest with the three-band rule; the pick-type control is one pre-registered pooled test (P7) with no per-cell tests, so no multiplicity correction is needed. Poison validity is mechanical (replay failure), not judged; the compiler audit is descriptive. Prefill tokens per episode logged for cached (R2-R6) and uncached (R1) prefixes; results plotted on the accuracy-cost plane. Pre-registration of arms, cells, margins, the exposure and audit rubrics, the cut order and the stopping rule before the first confirmatory cell; decoding, max steps and games identical across arms.

Risk Factors and Limitations: If the poison is inert (P1 falsified) the study ends with a negative that is itself useful for the compliance-trap literature; a weak poison (loss in [12, 20)) downgrades P2-P6 to exploratory by the pre-registered rule rather than being absorbed. The LLM compiler may correct the sample from pretraining knowledge; P3b then counts as falsified and the audit names the route, with the rule compiler as the clean aggregator reference. Fabricated poison is a stylised contamination; the stale-item realism cell is exploratory only. Contamination is applied to three types, so the primary cell is half the games; the pooled and 4-seed cells bring the decisive floors to +-5 to +-10 but each single-draw cell remains at +-12. Only Qwen3-32B as reader and compiler; compliance may differ by backbone. The R6 cross puts an instruction and exemplars in the same prompt, a format none of the single-slot arms uses, so its absolute levels are compared within the cross and against k=0 only. Whole-bank realised contamination varies by sample and is recorded as a covariate. Exposure being p per slot is by construction and is not claimed as a finding. Thirds rather than quarters were chosen so exact compositions exist for k=3 and three-exemplar sets; the compiler threshold is therefore located between one-in-three and two-in-three, not more finely, and the 50/50 hedging cell is deferred.
Addresses gap: G2 (whether a retriever contributes anything beyond a fixed exemplar set or a static playbook is not isolated; no random/fixed exemplar controls): fixed-sample, compiled, whole-bank and combined static routes are compared with retrieval at every contamination level, each with its own p=0 baseline; G4 (run-to-run variance unreported): compile-draw variance (three draws) and sample-draw variance (five draws at the decisive composition) are measured and folded into the CI; cross-axis G15 (asymmetry of right vs wrong retrieved memory) is dosed rather than named, and the slot-conflict cross puts right and wrong content in the same prompt.
Not a restatement of: Prior-result bullet 'Two pools on disk (expert 1,465; self 1,892 successes ...)': the pools are taken as given there; this idea manipulates the bank's contamination rate and claims that the routes differ in the shape of their response, which a clean bank cannot show. Digest card arxiv:2607.10608 (compliance trap: agents adopt conflicting retrieved memory; whether static instructions induce the same is untested): this idea answers that question with p manipulated and compiled, whole-bank, fixed-sample and slot-conflict routes on the same cells, and claims a step response for compilation (flat at one-in-three, collapse at two-in-three) against a linear one for retrieval and fixed exemplars, plus a wrong instruction followed at least as readily as wrong exemplars.
Changes made: P1: the k=0 clause removed from the gate and made descriptive; a three-band rule (>= 20 pass, < 12 stop, [12, 20) weak poison with P2-P6 exploratory and margins rescaled to fractions of the p=1 loss) states what happens between. P2: claim unchanged; realised per-episode exposure logged and the conditional loss reported as secondary; both R1 cells at 4 seeds. P3: both falsifiers now rest on success numbers alone (draw-pooled cells; 90% CI bound for the flat half, point loss for the collapse half); the audit is a descriptive covariate and a compiler-prior restoration counts as falsification instead of a confound; R2_p0 x3 funded in the count. P4: falsifier stated on R4 alone (loss < 12 vs R4_p0), no conjunction with P2; R4_p0 funded. P5: the floored p=1 contrast replaced by a slot-conflict 2x2 (R6: wrong instruction + clean exemplars vs clean instruction + wrong exemplars, plus clean + clean) at 4 seeds, so instruction compliance is measured where neither cell is floored and the dissociation the check asked for is isolated. P6: two sampled draws replaced by exact-composition R5 cells (j wrong in three) with five draws at j=1; the spread claim became a compliance claim on pooled j=1 vs j=0, and the equivalence with R1_p1/3 uses a 90% CI whose half-width (~9) is below the +-12 margin so noise alone does not satisfy it. P7: the 32-way conjunction replaced by one pre-registered pooled regression with a +-8 falsifier and no per-cell tests. Grid: quarters replaced by thirds (p in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1}) so exact compositions exist for k=3 and the static p=0 cells and extra draws fit the envelope; the p=.5 hedging cell cut. Budget restated with arithmetic: 37 cells x 548 = 20,276 episodes, ~18.5 h on two A100s, pre-registered cut order that never touches P1-P4 cells. Sharpness kept: the central claims (compliance at one-in-three for retrieval, fixed exemplars and whole bank; a step for the compiler; instruction slot no safer than exemplar slot) remain directional point predictions with the same 12/20 margins, none conditioned on another prediction's outcome or on an audit, and R6 makes the slot claim a stronger test than the floored p=1 contrast it replaces; no objection was answered by dropping a route or hedging the hypothesis.

Name: many_shot_averages_detours
Title: Reading the Whole Bank Averages Out Detours: Many-Shot Context Is Robust to Per-Item Noise Where Top-k Retrieval Commits to It
Short Hypothesis: When the bank holds the agent's own successful-but-detoured trajectories (self pool) instead of expert trajectories, top-k retrieval passes the detours of the items it commits to (the rank-1 item above all) into the episode (more steps, more step-limit failures, lower success), while the whole-bank route is insensitive to the detour rate because the shared procedure is the consensus across many noisy items and idiosyncratic detours have no consensus; the gap between routes grows with the bank's detour rate and with item count, and closes when detours (not merely tokens) are pruned from the items.
Related Work: Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) report that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the most similar examples rather than cumulative learning, and arxiv:2412.16926 that long-context models are less sensitive to example selection; both predict that a whole-bank prompt inherits whatever its most similar item contains, the opposite of consensus reading. In-context learning with noisy labels (arxiv:2411.19581) and many-shot ICL (arxiv:2404.11018, including Unsupervised and Reinforced ICL with model-generated examples) study label noise in classification, not action noise in trajectories. ExpeL and SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) reuse raw on-policy trajectories and report episode-specific drift and clutter from larger libraries without stating how items were selected; Honest Lying (arxiv:2605.29463) shows reflexive agents storing confident wrong interpretations; MemoryGraft (arxiv:2512.16962) and the compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) show agents imitating implanted or conflicting retrieved experiences. None sets the detour rate of a trajectory bank at several levels and compares whole-bank reading with top-k retrieval on task success and steps.
Abstract: Long-context in-context learning studies report that gains from many demonstrations come from attention to the most similar examples rather than from cumulative learning, which predicts that reading a whole bank of trajectories inherits whatever the most similar item contains. We test the opposite on agent trajectories, where per-item noise has a natural form: the detours in the agent's own successful episodes. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we build banks from the expert pool (no detours), the self pool (every item detoured), a high-detour self pool matched to the self pool on type and expert solution length, a pruned self pool whose detour visits are removed by rule and re-validated by replay, and a sham-pruned pool built from the same items with the same number of tokens removed elsewhere and every detour kept. Each bank is read by goal-sentence top-3 retrieval or whole in a cached prefix at 6, 24 and 48 items, on the same 274 games and two seeds; whole-bank prefixes are drawn per game block so that the most-similar item's detour and the bank-mean detour vary within an arm. Two composition arms put a self item at rank 1 only, or at ranks 2-3 only, of an otherwise expert triple. We score success, steps and step-limit failures against the Measurement C static arms and a self-pool static3. We predict that retrieval passes detours into the episode through the rank-1 item, that the whole-bank route is insensitive to the detour rate and improves with item count on the self pool only, that pruning restores retrieval where the sham-prune does not, and that whole-bank episodes do not track the most-similar item's detours within a pre-registered slope bound. Costs under caching are measured, since the robust route is also the longer prefix.
Experiments:
- Pools and banks. E: expert pool (1,465). S: self pool (1,892 successes). Per item: detour steps = steps beyond the expert solution length for the same game; detour visits = receptacle visits that did not yield the target object plus repeated identical actions; distributions reported by type and by expert-solution-length tercile. A: within each stratum (type x expert-solution-length tercile) the top tercile of S by detour steps, with stratum weights equal to S's, so A matches S on type and difficulty and differs only in detour steps. P: pruned S, detour visits deleted, the pruned action list replayed in the same game, only successful replays kept; P's coverage of S by stratum is reported. Sh: sham-pruned S, built from exactly P's source items and matched to P's token count per item (within 10 percent) by deleting state-neutral non-detour steps (look, inventory, examine, redundant go-to) and then shortening observation strings of non-detour steps, with every detour visit and its observation kept; replay-verified. Item tokens measured (E about 140; S expected about 2x; P about E; Sh equal to P).
- Routes. RET: goal-sentence top-3 (the Measurement A retriever), uncached; per episode the retrieved item ids, ranks, lengths and detour steps are logged. Composition arms: M1 = the top S item at rank 1 followed by the top-2 E items; M2 = the top E item at rank 1 followed by the top-2 S items (same retriever, same games). WB: whole bank as a type-agnostic cached static prefix. Block design: the 274 games are split into 8 type-stratified blocks (about 34 games each); each block gets its own random type-balanced bank drawn from the pool, and S banks are drawn with a tilt (2 blocks from the bottom tercile of detour steps within type, 4 uniform, 2 from the top tercile) so the bank-mean detour spans the pool's range while the arm mean equals the pool mean; episodes run block by block so one prefix is hot at a time. Rungs: E at 6 and 48 items, S at 6, 24 and 48. Fit rule fixed before the run: the top rung is 48 if a 48-item S prefix plus a 3k-token history reserve fits 16k, otherwise the largest multiple of 6 that fits, used for both pools. Token-matched comparison WB E48 vs WB S24 also reported.
- Static arm on the self pool. static3-S: 3 fixed type-conditioned S exemplars (the S counterpart of Measurement C's static3), cached.
- Arms at Qwen3-32B, each 274 games x 2 seeds = 548 episodes paired on (game, seed) with Measurements A and C: RET S, RET A, RET P, RET Sh, RET M1, RET M2, static3-S, WB E6, WB E48, WB S6, WB S24, WB S48: 12 arms, 6,576 episodes, about 8 h on two GPUs at the Measurement C rate (about 40 min per 548-episode arm on two replicas). Conditional extra arm: RET S_P (the unpruned versions of P's surviving items) if fewer than 80 percent of S items survive pruning (+40 min). RET E is Measurement A; k0 and the static arms are Measurement C.
- Outcomes: success (primary), steps per episode and step-limit failures (secondary, paired). Mechanism regressions: in RET arms, the per-(game, seed) step difference against RET E regressed on the injected items' detour steps (rank-1 item and mean over 3); in WB48 S, the same difference against WB48 E regressed on the detour steps of the most-similar prefix item (by retriever score, varying per game) and on the block bank-mean detour steps (8 tilted values, block-level bootstrap). Exploratory consensus signature: whether the episode visits the type's modal wrong receptacle (the receptacle most often visited without yield across S items of that type) regressed on that receptacle's share among the block bank's items and on whether the most-similar item visits it.
- Reader: Qwen3-8B on RET E, RET S, WB48 E, WB48 S as an exploratory replication of the 2x2 (4 arms, about 1 h).
- Cost: prefill tokens and GPU-seconds per episode under prefix caching (8 prefixes per WB arm, one hot at a time); detours lengthen episodes and multiply decode steps, so cost per success is reported for both routes.
- Order: RET S, then the positive control RET A vs RET S (stop rule); pre-registration including the slope MDE from measured step and detour SDs; then WB48 E and WB48 S (the 2x2 with RET E, RET S); then static3-S; then the S ladder and WB E6; then P and Sh; then M1 and M2; then Qwen3-8B.
Baselines and Ablations:
- k0 and the Measurement C static arms (static3, procedure paragraph, six-procedure instr_all, wrong-type blind1); every retrieval number is reported in the brief's residual form, retrieval minus the best static arm built from the same pool at matched tokens: for E, static3 (k3 - static3 = +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4]) or WB48 E, whichever is higher; for S, static3-S or WB48 S, whichever is higher.
- RET E (Measurement A) is the clean-item reference.
- A is the positive control, matched to S on type and expert solution length so the contrast varies detour steps only. P is the repair ablation; Sh is its length control (same items, same tokens removed, detours kept), so P vs Sh isolates detour content from token count and P vs E on covered games isolates phrasing.
- M1 and M2 are the composition ablations: same retriever, same games, self item at rank 1 only or at ranks 2-3 only.
- static3-S is the few-fixed-items counterpart of RET S: it tests whether few detoured items inherit detours whether or not they were retrieved.
- WB E at 6 and 48 is the no-noise reference for the S ladder (6, 24, 48); the tilted block banks give the whole-bank route a within-arm detour-rate dose at fixed item count.
- Token-matched WB E48 vs WB S24 controls for the longer S items.
- Type conditioning: WB prefixes are type-agnostic; static3-S is type-conditioned like static3; RET selects by goal sentence.

Name: binding_scope_leakage_ladder
Title: Global Fact, Scene Table, or Instance Replay: The Scope of Instance Bindings Sets How Much of a Memory Gain Is Near-Duplicate Leakage and Whether a Static Prompt Can Match It
Short Hypothesis: An experience bank helps on a new task instance only through information that transfers from bank items to that instance. The scope of the instance bindings (global = per object class, per scene, per instance) fixes both the smallest static substitute for retrieval and the share of the retrieval gain that is near-duplicate leakage: at class scope one sentence per class matches scene-query retrieval and one bank item per class suffices; at scene scope one static (scene, class) table matches it; at instance scope no static prefix smaller than one row per instance exists, the gain exists only through the instance's own duplicate, it is linear in the duplicate rate because duplicates neither spill over to non-duplicated instances nor get discounted when rare, and a whole-bank prefix that contains the duplicate cannot replace the query. The natural ALFWorld bank sits at class scope (unseen >= seen), so its measured +17.2 net residual over the best static arm (static3) compiles into about 20 class-location sentences.
Related Work: Evo-Memory (arXiv:2511.20857) and ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) measure memory as test-time evolution over task streams without reporting how much of the gain comes from near-duplicate tasks within the stream. EvoMemBench (arXiv:2605.18421) organizes memory by scope (in-episode vs cross-episode) and content, and finds long-context baselines outperform memory methods, but does not manipulate binding scope or duplicate rate. AgentCL (arXiv:2606.02461) builds controlled task streams with transfer-gain metrics, without a compiled-prompt arm or a scope manipulation. SWE-ContextBench (arXiv:2602.08316) draws related tasks from dependency links (observed relatedness). The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows adoption of wrong retrieved memory. In the home literature, deduplication of training data (arXiv:2107.06499) and contamination analyses (ConTAM arXiv:2411.03923; rephrased-sample contamination arXiv:2311.04850) quantify score inflation from near-duplicate overlap for pretraining, never for experience banks. Archived order_randomized_leakage_audit audited leakage by order randomization (observed); Measurements A and C (unseen >= seen; k3 - static3 = +17.2 net at the natural bank) are the starting point.
Abstract: Memory benchmarks differ in what an experience bank can transfer to a new instance: a rule that holds everywhere (per object class), a binding that holds within a scene, or a binding that holds only for the instance itself, which the bank contains only if the instance recurs. We manipulate this scope on ALFWorld with the relocation machinery (target objects moved off their canonical receptacle, 25-step budget) under three relocation rules: global (every instance of a class goes to one receptacle type in every scene), scene (per (scene, class)), instance (per game). Supply is the fraction s of eval games whose scope unit is covered in the bank: at scene scope s in {0, 1} (same-scene relocated sibling present or not); at instance scope s in {0, 0.5, 1}, where the duplicate is the PDDL expert's trajectory for the eval game's own relocated init, so every game carries one independent of any baseline outcome; at global scope the full relocated bank versus a 20-item one-per-class bank. Arms per scope: scene-query retrieval k=3; the reference static arm static3-relocated (three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars rebuilt from the relocated bank; Measurement C's best static arm); the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt; the scope's compiled static arm (one sentence per class at global scope; one static prefix holding every (scene, class) row at scene scope; none at instance scope, where no prefix smaller than one row per instance exists); and the whole-bank arm (20 items in context at global scope; the scene-restricted bank, <= 80 items in fixed order, at scene and instance scope). Every retrieval number is reported minus static3-relocated and minus the best static arm on the same (game, seed), with cached and uncached prefill tokens. The leakage index at a scope is the part of the retrieval residual removed by deleting scope-matched duplicates; at instance scope the s=0.5 condition is run as two complementary draws so that the residual on duplicated games D(0.5) and on non-duplicated games N(0.5) each have the full n. A natural-bank anchor cell tests whether Measurement C's +17.2 residual over static3 compiles into a class-location table. Predictions: a sentence matches retrieval at class scope, a row table at scene scope, nothing but the duplicate at instance scope; D(0.5) equals the s=1 residual and N(0.5) equals the s=0 residual (linear in s, no spillover, no discounting); an 80-item whole bank that contains the duplicate loses >= 14 net to the query at instance scope; each prediction names the cell that can refute it.
Experiments: 1. Gate (pre-registered, the positive control shared with the relocation design): scene scope, s=1, relocated x 25-step: scene-query retrieval minus static3-relocated >= +14 net; if it fails the ladder is not run and the failure is reported. 2. Construction: three relocation rules applied to the PDDL init of the 274 eval games and of the train games in eval scenes; expert trajectories regenerated with the ALFWorld PDDL expert (CPU); instance-scope duplicates are the expert trajectories of the eval games' own relocated inits, placed in the bank for a fraction s of games (s=0.5 as two complementary seed-drawn halves A and B); static3-relocated is rebuilt per scope from the relocated bank with the same three exemplar slots as Measurement C; the compiled sentence and table are written by rule from the bank; eval games sharing (goal text, scene) with another eval game are counted and form the tied subset. 3. Natural-bank anchor (1 cell): class-location table static (one sentence per class listing the receptacles where that class was picked in the natural train bank, <= 430 tokens, cached), paired against Measurement C's k3 and static3 rows on the same (game, seed) under Measurement C settings (k3 re-run as one extra cell if the vLLM build changed). 4. Confirmatory cells, each 274 games x 2 seeds = 548 episodes: scene scope (6): retrieval s=1, retrieval s=0, static3-relocated, type-agnostic, table static, whole-bank; global scope (6): retrieval full bank, retrieval 20-item bank, static3-relocated, type-agnostic, compiled sentence, whole-bank-20; instance scope (7): retrieval s=1, s=0.5 draw A, s=0.5 draw B, s=0, static3-relocated, type-agnostic, whole-bank. 5. Exploratory (2 cells): on-policy self-duplicate at instance scope s=1 (the game's own verified success from the type-agnostic cell, which doubles as the first pass; solved games only) versus the expert duplicate; stale duplicate (the same game's canonical pre-relocation expert trajectory) at instance scope s=1. Logged without episodes: rank of the self-duplicate under scene-query and goal-query. 6. Arithmetic: 20 confirmatory + 2 exploratory (+1 optional k3 re-run) = 22-23 cells x 548 = 12.1k-12.6k episodes; at Measurement C's throughput (~19 episodes/min on two A100s, one vLLM replica per GPU) about 10.5-11 h, static cells faster because their prefixes are cached. 7. Cost: cached and uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock per episode; accuracy-cost curve per scope.
Baselines and Ablations: Static (cached, byte-identical prefixes): static3-relocated (reference static arm at every scope; three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars rebuilt from each scope's relocated bank, ~430 tokens); type-agnostic six-procedure prompt (no bindings; run at every scope, controls type conditioning); compiled sentence per class (global scope, ~20 sentences); compiled (scene, class) table as one static prefix (scene scope, <= 274 rows); class-location table (natural bank); whole-bank: the 20-item one-per-class bank in context at global scope, the scene-restricted bank at scene and instance scope (all bank items from the eval game's scene, <= 80 in fixed game-id order, the eval game's own duplicate included at instance scope s=1; banks over 80 items drop train items by highest game id first and counts are reported). Retrieval: scene-query k=3 (goal plus first observation), the Measurement C retriever; ablations: 20-item one-per-class bank versus the full relocated bank at global scope; s=0 at scene and instance scope (scope-matched duplicates deleted); s=0.5 in two complementary draws at instance scope; stale and on-policy duplicates at instance scope (exploratory). Per the rules every retrieval cell is reported minus static3-relocated and minus the best static arm of its scope (max over the static arms above by pooled success). Dropped from the previous version: the global s=0 cell (P3 carries the global leakage claim), the k=1 and k=7 sweeps, and the random-type length placebo (Measurement C's blind1 bounds the length effect at -3 net).
Falsifiable Predictions: Margins follow the brief: the +-8 net floor at 274 x 2 is the smallest reportable difference and +14 is the confirmatory margin. P0 (natural-bank anchor, stated against Measurement C's k3 - static3 = +17.2 [+11.9, +22.4]) The class-location table static minus k3 >= -8 net on the natural bank, i.e. the table recovers at least +9 of the +17.2 over static3. Falsified by table - k3 < -8 in the anchor cell (the +17.2 is scene-family information a class sentence cannot carry; the natural bank then sits between class and scene scope). P1 (gate) At scene scope, s=1, retrieval minus static3-relocated >= +14 net. Falsified by < +8 in that cell; the ladder is then not run. P2 (class scope compiles to a sentence) Positive control read first: at global scope retrieval (full bank) minus static3-relocated >= +14, falsified by < +8 (the reader does not carry a class rule out of other-scene trajectories), in which case P2 and P3 are reported as not testable. P2 proper: compiled-sentence static minus retrieval >= -8 net. Falsified by sentence < retrieval - 8 in the sentence cell (the reader applies a concrete trajectory but not a stated rule). P3 (one item per class suffices) At global scope retrieval with the 20-item bank is within +-8 of retrieval with the full relocated bank. Falsified by 20-item < full - 8 in the 20-item cell (a many-shot per-class requirement). P4 (scene scope compiles to a table) Table static minus retrieval (s=1) >= -8 net at scene scope. Falsified by table < retrieval - 8 in the table cell (the reader cannot look up its scene's row among <= 274). P5 (instance scope: an exact duplicate is replayed) At instance scope, retrieval (s=1, expert self-duplicate present) minus static3-relocated >= +28 net. Falsified by < +20 (95% CI excluding +28) in that cell (the reader does not follow even its own instance's expert trajectory within 25 steps, or k=3 does not rank it first). P6 (headline: the instance-scope gain is the duplicate and nothing else) Read if residual(1) >= +14. At instance scope s=0.5, pooled over the two complementary draws so each term has n = 274 x 2: the residual on games whose duplicate is present, D(0.5), is >= residual(1) - 8, and the residual on games whose duplicate is absent, N(0.5), is <= residual(0) + 8; since the pooled residual at s equals s x D(s) + (1 - s) x N(s), this is the linear-in-s law with intercept residual(0). Falsified by D(0.5) <= residual(1) - 14 (discounting: the reader trusts a duplicate less when half of the bank's retrievals are non-duplicates; s=0.5 cells against the s=1 cell) or by N(0.5) >= residual(0) + 14 (spillover: other games' duplicates in the bank seed a search strategy that transfers to non-duplicated games; s=0.5 cells against the s=0 cell). residual(0) is a measured anchor, not a claim. P7 (the whole bank does not replace the query at instance scope) At instance scope s=1, the scene-restricted whole-bank arm (<= 80 items, the game's own duplicate among them) <= retrieval - 14 net. Falsified by whole-bank >= retrieval - 8 in that cell (the reader finds its own instance among 80 same-scene trajectories without a query). Shared terms: P5, P6 and P7 use the instance-scope s=1 retrieval cell, and P6 is read only when residual(1) >= +14; P1 and P4 share the scene-scope s=1 retrieval cell; P2 and P3 share the global full-bank cell.
Measurement and Noise Control: Task success on identical (game, seed) pairs across arms within each scope; paired nets with a cluster bootstrap over games (1,000 resamples) and 95% CIs; the +-8 net floor at 274 x 2 is the minimum reportable margin, +14 the confirmatory margin (half the Gate-0 gain), and P5 uses +28 with its falsifier at +20 so that a 14-point discount in P6 is a reportable loss. The reference static arm is pre-registered as static3-relocated per scope; retrieval minus the best static arm of the scope is also reported for every cell. The s=0.5 draws are complementary halves of the 274 games, so D(0.5) and N(0.5) are each measured on every game once at each seed (n = 274 x 2, floor +-8) and do not depend on which games carry duplicates; the same expert duplicates are used in every instance-scope arm. Eval games tied on (goal text, scene) with another eval game are counted; the primary instance-scope analysis is on untied games and the tied subset is reported separately. Same decoding, vLLM build, prompt template and retriever as Measurement C; static prefixes byte-identical with cache hits verified from logs; cached and uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock per episode logged. Gate and P0-P7 pre-registered before the first confirmatory cell; per-type claims exploratory; valid_seen and valid_unseen reported separately and pooled.

Name: near_duplicate_needle_crossover
Title: Bigger Banks Help Retrieval Only Through Near-Duplicates the Reader Cannot Find in Context: Bank Size x Near-Duplicate Rate on WebShop and ALFWorld
Short Hypothesis: The growth of top-k retrieval's advantage over the whole-bank-in-context route with bank size is a near-duplicate effect. On WebShop (one procedure, instance-specific product and option bindings), with near-duplicates replaced by same-category trajectories that share no bindings, retrieval, the whole bank and the best static prompt are within the noise floor at every bank size; with near-duplicates planted, retrieval's gain rises with the planted rate, requires the needle to be retrieved (a needle present in the bank but unretrievable by instruction text gives retrieval nothing), and the whole-bank route recovers less than half of it, the recovered fraction falling as the haystack grows from 12 to 40 items with the distractor composition held fixed. On ALFWorld the measured +17.2 net residual of retrieval over the best static arm is carried by near-duplicates at the binding level the goal sentence exposes (task type, object, receptacle): removing them removes at least half of the residual, while the same-scene manipulation (bindings the goal sentence does not expose) leaves retrieval unmoved.
Related Work: Synapse (arxiv:2306.07863) introduced trajectory-as-exemplar prompting with state abstraction and an exemplar memory retrieved by similarity on MiniWoB++ and Mind2Web, without a whole-bank or random-selection control; ExpeL and Agent Workflow Memory likewise assume retrieval over experience on WebShop-style tasks. arxiv:2603.18272 trains agents to use retrieved trajectories without a fixed or random exemplar control. Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) find that long-context ICL gains come from attention to similar examples so that random many-shot converges to retrieval on classification, and arxiv:2412.16926 that selection matters less with long context; arxiv:2411.05000 shows in-context lookup degrading with context on synthetic threads. arxiv:2607.26497 sweeps corpus size on documents with one reader and scores recall. The archived order_randomized_leakage_audit observed near-duplicate leakage in task streams, and decorative_retriever observed that retrieval-set overlap predicts retrieval necessity; neither planted or removed near-duplicates or ran a whole-bank arm. The home Measurement C (runs/STEP0_RESULTS.md) measured k3 minus the best static arm (static3, three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars) at +17.2 net on ALFWorld's natural bank, with unseen (+20.1) above seen (+14.3); it observed the natural pool and did not manipulate it.
Abstract: Bank-size sweeps in retrieval are done on document corpora with one reader and scored on recall; for agent experience banks the operative question is why a larger bank helps retrieval at all, and whether the whole bank in context would do the same. We hypothesise that the bank-size curve of top-k retrieval on trajectory banks is a near-duplicate coverage curve, and that the whole-bank route's curve is an in-context lookup curve that falls as the haystack grows. On WebShop (one procedure, instance-specific product and option bindings) we build per-cluster banks of state-abstracted successful trajectories at 12 and 40 items in which the fraction of test instructions with a near-duplicate (same product, or same category with two shared attribute phrases) is 0, 0.5 or 1, the remaining slots filled by same-category trajectories that share no attribute phrase with any cluster instruction, with the filler set held fixed across sizes; a hidden-needle variant keeps the near-duplicate in the bank but makes it unretrievable by instruction text. Banks are read by instruction-text top-2 retrieval, whole in a cached prefix, or through fixed-exemplar and compiled-procedure static prompts. On ALFWorld the same manipulation is applied at the binding level the goal sentence exposes (task type, object, receptacle) and, on seen scenes, at the scene level, and is stated against the measured +17.2 net residual of retrieval over the best static arm. We predict no retrieval residual over the best static arm or the whole bank without near-duplicates, a residual that requires the needle to be retrieved, a whole-bank recovery below half that shrinks from 12 to 40 items, and on ALFWorld a residual at least halved by removing binding-level near-duplicates while the scene-level manipulation leaves retrieval unmoved. Task success is primary, needle hit and needle-use rates are mediators, and cost is measured under prefix caching.
Experiments:
- WebShop setup (public data; about a day of install). Reader Qwen3-32B, one vLLM replica per GPU with prefix caching. Evaluation on the standard 500 test instructions; confirmatory cells at 4 seeds (2,000 paired episodes), secondary cells at 2 seeds; identical seeds and instruction order across arms. The k=0 arm runs first at 4 seeds and its seeds 1-2 versus 3-4 difference sets the paired floor (expected about +/-3 points of success at 2,000 episodes, about +/-4.5 at 1,000).
- Bank material: successes (reward 1.0) of Qwen3-32B on at least 2,000 train instructions (expected 600-800 items) plus the public human demonstrations; Synapse-style state abstraction (search pages reduced to the top-5 result lines of item id, title and price; product pages to title, price, options and the buy action) applied identically to retrieved and whole-bank items; items truncated to 300 tokens (the stated truncation rule), so a 40-item prefix is about 12k tokens and fits 16k with the episode.
- Needles (near-duplicates) for a test instruction: a bank trajectory whose instruction targets the same product id, or the same top-level category with at least two shared attribute phrases. Because WebShop has about one instruction per product, same-product needles are constructed: a paraphrased instruction for the test product (attribute subset, different price cap) is run to success (up to 3 attempts) and the success kept. Same-product and shared-attribute needles are reported separately, and the gain as a function of shared-attribute count. Test instructions without a constructible needle are dropped from every cell (paired set; expected at least 450 retained; the floor is re-measured on the retained set).
- Clusters: retained instructions are grouped into clusters of 5 from the same top-level category with pairwise-disjoint attribute phrases (about 90 clusters), so each needle is a near-duplicate of exactly one cluster instruction. Fillers (sib-0) are same-top-level-category train trajectories whose instructions share no attribute phrase with any cluster instruction; each cluster draws one 35-item filler set once, and the 7-item filler set used at size 12 is a subset of it, so distractor composition is identical across sizes and only the count varies. Cells at size 40: r=1 is 5 needles + 35 fillers; r=0.5 is 2 or 3 needles (alternating by cluster) + fillers to 40; r=0 is 40 fillers. Size 12: r=1 is 5 needles + 7 fillers; r=0 is 12 fillers. Hidden-needle (r=1h): the r=1 bank with each needle's instruction line replaced by the category template line ('I am looking for a [category] item'), trajectory body unchanged; the retrieval index is built on instruction lines only, so the needle's retrievability drops to chance (its top-2 hit rate is logged; expected near 0.05).
- Routes: WB-12 and WB-40 (the cluster bank as a cached static prefix, warmed once per cluster per seed and scheduled cluster-by-cluster); RET-2 (top-2 from the same cluster bank by BM25 plus embedding over instruction lines, uncached; needle hit rate logged); static arms: fixed-2 (two fixed sib-0 items from one category, identical for all clusters, cached), compiled (one procedure paragraph: search, pick, options, buy; cached), k=0. Best static is the highest of the three at matched tokens; every retrieval or whole-bank number is reported against it.
- WebShop arms and counts. 4 seeds (2,000 episodes each): k=0, fixed-2, RET-40 r=0, RET-40 r=1, WB-40 r=0, WB-40 r=1, WB-12 r=0, WB-12 r=1 (8 arms, 16,000 episodes). 2 seeds (1,000 each): compiled (extended to 4 seeds if it beats fixed-2), RET-40 r=0.5, RET-12 r=1, RET-40 r=1h, WB-40 r=1h (5 arms, 5,000-6,000 episodes). Exploratory reader (G16): Qwen3-8B on k=0, RET-40 r=0, RET-40 r=1, WB-40 r=0, WB-40 r=1 at 1 seed (2,500 episodes). About 24,000 episodes at about 1,000 per hour on two GPUs: about 24 h, plus about 3 h of bank and needle construction.
- ALFWorld (installed; Measurement C reader and serving). Bank items: train expert trajectories at about 140 tokens each. Binding levels for a test game: full = same (task type, object class, receptacle class); partial = same type and one of the two; none = same type, different object and receptacle. Per-game banks at 72 items (12 per task type, type-agnostic composition): r=1 holds one full-match item for the test game (from a different scene) plus 11 none-level same-type items and 12 items per other type; r=0 replaces the full-match item by a twelfth none-level item, with no full or partial match anywhere in the bank. Scene cells on the valid_seen games that have a same-scene full-match train item (expected at least 90): scene-r1 uses that item as the needle; scene-r0 uses a different-scene full-match item, all else equal. Routes: RET k=3 by goal text over the bank (as k3 in Measurement C) and WB-72 as a cached per-game prefix (about 10k tokens); static3 (Measurement C's best static arm) re-run on the added seeds so every contrast is paired on the same (game, seed).
- ALFWorld arms and counts. 274 games x 4 seeds (1,096 each): RET-72 r=0, RET-72 r=1, WB-72 r=0, WB-72 r=1, plus static3 on seeds 3-4 (548): 4,932 episodes. Scene cells: 2 arms x (at least 90 games x 4-6 seeds), about 1,200. Exploratory at 274 x 2: WB-24 r=1 (4 per type; the haystack-size replicate of P3b) and RET-72 r=partial (binding ladder): 1,096. About 7,200 episodes at about 730 per hour: about 10 h.
- Outcomes: success (WebShop reward = 1; ALFWorld success) primary; WebShop mean reward secondary; mediators logged per episode: needle hit rate in the retrieved set, needle-use rate (the episode's chosen product id or first search query equals the needle's; on ALFWorld, the first navigation target equals the needle's object location), prefill tokens.
- Cost: prefill tokens, cache hit ratio per cluster or game, GPU-seconds per episode; accuracy-cost frontier across static, retrieval and whole-bank arms per rate.
- Order: install; k=0 at 4 seeds and floor; bank and needles; positive control P1 (RET-40 r=1 vs r=0 at 4 seeds; gate at least 15 points, else stop); pre-registration of floor, gain and margins; remaining WebShop confirmatory cells; ALFWorld confirmatory cells interleaved on the second replica; secondary cells; 8B. Total about 34 GPU-hours across two A100s after install.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Static arms as the baseline on WebShop: fixed-2 (cached), compiled procedure paragraph (cached), k=0; every retrieval and whole-bank number is reported as the arm minus the best static arm at matched tokens on the same (instruction, seed). On ALFWorld the best static arm is static3 from Measurement C (+12.4 over k0), re-run on the added seeds; the type-agnostic instr_all number from Measurement C is the type-conditioning reference.
- Whole-bank at two haystack sizes (12 and 40 on WebShop; 72 confirmatory and 24 exploratory on ALFWorld) is the matched-budget no-retriever arm, with filler composition identical across sizes; the r=0 banks are the fixed-selection control at the whole-context budget.
- Near-duplicate rate ladder 0/0.5/1 on retrieval at size 40 (0.5 secondary); shared-attribute count and same-product versus shared-attribute needles as graded near-duplicate strength.
- Hidden-needle bank (needle present, instruction line templated) on both routes: separates needle presence from retrievability, and tests whether the whole-bank route's lookup depends on the instruction line.
- Retrieval at fixed rate across sizes (RET-12 r=1 vs RET-40 r=1): separates the coverage curve from a hit-rate curve.
- ALFWorld binding ladder (full / partial / none) and the scene manipulation with the full match held fixed: which bindings the residual over static3 is made of.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (positive control and gate; near-duplicates, not category material, carry the gain): on WebShop at size 40 with 4 seeds, RET-40 r=1 minus RET-40 r=0, where the r=0 bank holds 40 same-category items sharing no attribute phrase with any cluster instruction and the r=1 bank swaps five of them for the cluster's needles, is at least 15 points of success. Falsified if the difference is within the floor (about +/-3): the retriever's most similar sibling transfers search wording and product-page procedure as well as the needle does, and the design stops; a difference between the floor and 15 points fails the gate and the design stops without a claim. Arms: RET-40 r=1, RET-40 r=0.
- P2 (no residual without near-duplicates): at r=0, RET-40 minus the best static arm and RET-40 minus WB-40 r=0 are each within the floor. Falsified if either exceeds one third of the P1 gain (at least 5 points at the gate, above the floor): the retriever's choice among same-category siblings carries category-level wording that neither a fixed exemplar nor the whole bank supplies. Between the floor and one third: undecided and reported. Arms: RET-40 r=0, WB-40 r=0, fixed-2, compiled, k=0.
- P3 (headline: the reader cannot find the needle, and finds it less as the haystack grows): with filler composition identical at both sizes, (a) WB-40's recovery of the near-duplicate gain, (WB-40 r=1 minus WB-40 r=0) over (RET-40 r=1 minus RET-40 r=0), has a paired-bootstrap upper bound below 0.5; (b) WB-12 r=1 exceeds WB-40 r=1 by at least one third of the P1 gain (the same five needles among 7 versus 35 fillers); (c) the needle-use rate is at least 20 points lower in WB-40 r=1 than in RET-40 r=1, with WB-12 r=1 at least 10 points above WB-40 r=1. Falsified if the recovery fraction's lower bound exceeds 0.5, or the needle-use rate in WB-40 r=1 is within its floor (about +/-3) of RET-40 r=1's (the reader locates the needle: the arxiv:2405.00200 outcome on trajectories), or WB-12 r=1 minus WB-40 r=1 is within the floor (haystack size between 12 and 40 does not matter). Decidable range: with a 15-point gain and a +/-3 floor the rule rejects 'below half' for true recoveries up to about 0.25; a recovery between 0.25 and 0.5 leaves an interval straddling 0.5 and is reported undecided; a larger measured gain widens the range and is pre-registered. Arms: WB-40 r=1, WB-40 r=0, WB-12 r=1, WB-12 r=0, RET-40 r=1, RET-40 r=0.
- P4 (the needle must be retrieved, not merely present): with the hidden-needle bank (needle present, instruction line templated, logged top-2 hit rate near 0.05), RET-40 r=1h minus RET-40 r=0 is within the floor, and WB-40 r=1h is within the floor of WB-40 r=1. Falsified if RET-40 r=1h retains at least half of the P1 gain (the retriever finds the needle from trajectory bodies, or siblings suffice once the needle is in the index), or if WB-40 r=1h falls below WB-40 r=1 by at least half of the gain (the whole-bank route's partial recovery is a lexical match on the instruction line, not a lookup over trajectory content). 2-seed cells, floor about +/-4.5, half of the gain is 7.5 points at the gate. Arms: RET-40 r=1h, WB-40 r=1h, RET-40 r=0, WB-40 r=1.
- P5 (ALFWorld, stated against Measurement C's +17.2 net residual of k3 over static3, CI half-width about 5): (a) binding level: with 274 games x 4 seeds (floor about +/-5.7 net), RET-72 r=0 (no full or partial match; same-type different-binding fillers only) minus static3 is below +8.6 net, i.e. removing binding-level near-duplicates removes at least half of the residual; RET-72 r=1 minus static3 is reported as a calibration and must exceed +8.6 for (a) to be interpretable. Falsified if RET-72 r=0 minus static3 is at least +12 net: the residual is carried by same-type exemplars with different bindings, ALFWorld is procedure-bound, and the near-duplicate account does not cover its retrieval gain. (b) scene level: on the valid_seen games with a same-scene full-match train item (seeds added until the paired floor is at most +/-8 net), RET scene-r1 minus RET scene-r0 is below +8 net; falsified if it is at least +12 net (bindings absent from the goal sentence matter after all). Arms: RET-72 r=0, RET-72 r=1, static3 (seeds 3-4 added), scene-r1, scene-r0. (c) exploratory, not confirmatory: WB-72 r=1's recovery of the binding-level residual with its interval, and WB-24 r=1 versus WB-72 r=1 as the haystack-size replicate of P3b.
- P6 (retrieval's curve is flat in size at fixed rate): RET-12 r=1 and RET-40 r=1 are within the floor of each other (2 seeds, about +/-4.5), with top-2 needle hit rate above 0.9 at both sizes. Falsified if RET-40 r=1 is below RET-12 r=1 by at least half of the P1 gain: the retriever loses the needle among 35 same-category fillers, the bank-size curve of retrieval is a hit-rate curve rather than a coverage curve, and the size effect is reported per logged hit rate. Arms: RET-12 r=1, RET-40 r=1.
- Secondary (reported, not confirmatory): RET-40 r=0.5's gain over r=0 as a fraction of the r=1 gain, expected near 0.5, with its interval.
Measurement and Noise Control: WebShop: paired per (instruction, seed) with identical seeds and instruction order across arms; confirmatory cells at 500 x 4 (expected floor about +/-3 points of success, measured before pre-registration as the k=0 seeds 1-2 versus 3-4 difference on the retained paired set), secondary cells at 500 x 2 (about +/-4.5); recovery fractions and needle-use rates carry paired-bootstrap intervals over instructions. Margins are fractions of the P1 gain (RET-40 r=1 minus RET-40 r=0, gate at least 15 points): confirmatory effects on 4-seed cells must exceed the floor and one third of that gain (5 points at the gate), on 2-seed cells half of it (7.5); an effect between the floor and its margin is reported undecided. P3's decision rule (bootstrap upper bound of the recovery fraction below 0.5) has power at true recoveries up to about 0.25 with a 15-point gain and a +/-3 floor; the decidable range is pre-registered from the measured gain. ALFWorld: 274 games x 4 seeds paired on (game, seed) with static3 re-run on the added seeds; floor about +/-5.7 net (the brief's +/-8 at 274 x 2 scaled by 1/sqrt(2)); margins stated against Measurement C's +17.2 (half is 8.6 net; falsifier at +12 net, above the floor); the scene subset adds seeds (4-6) until its paired floor is at most +/-8 net, with the falsifier at +12. Mediators (hit rate, needle-use rate) are per-episode binaries with floors near +/-3 at 2,000 episodes, secondary to success. Cost under prefix caching: prefill tokens, cache hit ratio per cluster or game, GPU-seconds per episode. Pre-registration after the floor and the positive control.
